chant.letra:
[Leader]
A scarf — wear it or carry it?
[Kids]
Wear it! Wear it round your neck!

[Leader]
A suitcase — wear it or carry it?
[Kids]
Carry it! Carry it, don't drop it!

[Leader]
A ring — wear it or carry it?
[Kids]
Wear it! On your finger!

[Leader]
An umbrella?
[Kids]
Carry it — and open it in time!

[All]
Gloves and belt and sunhat, socks —
pocket, uniform, and off we go!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Ingrid wears her uniform,
Diego carries his machine.
Maya's got a pocket full of stones
from every place she's been.

[Chorus]
You wear a scarf, you carry a case,
you put your gloves on when it's cold!
But what you carry all your life
is honesty, and that's worth gold!

[Verse 2]
A belt, a ring, a sunhat, socks,
an umbrella just in case.
Respect is not a thing you wear
but people see it on your face.

[Chorus]
You wear a scarf, you carry a case,
you put your gloves on when it's cold!
But what you carry all your life
is honesty, and that's worth gold!

[Bridge]
Wear it, carry it, put it on —
three small verbs and the day's begun.

[Chorus]
You wear a scarf, you carry a case,
you put your gloves on when it's cold!
But what you carry all your life
is honesty, and that's worth gold!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Where did you go?
[Kids]
We went to the museum!

[Leader]
What did you see?
[Kids]
We saw a castle! An old, old castle!

[Leader]
Where did you go after that?
[Kids]
The theatre! And the stadium!

[Leader]
And how was it?
[Kids]
It was brilliant! It was long!

[All]
Airport, bridge and funfair too —
went and saw and was, all true!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
We went down to the museum
and we saw a thousand years.
There was a room about the harbour
and it nearly brought us tears.

[Chorus]
We went, we saw, it was —
three small words that hold a day!
Castle, theatre, bridge and stadium,
and the whole long way!

[Verse 2]
Diego stopped at the police station
to ask about a local custom.
A tradition from the north, they said,
and nobody could trust him.

[Chorus]
We went, we saw, it was —
three small words that hold a day!
Castle, theatre, bridge and stadium,
and the whole long way!

[Bridge]
The airport, then the restaurant,
the chemist's for Maya's head.

[Chorus]
We went, we saw, it was —
three small words that hold a day!
Castle, theatre, bridge and stadium,
and the whole long way!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Have you found it yet?
[Kids]
Not yet! Not yet!

[Leader]
Have you looked in the bag?
[Kids]
Already! We've already looked!

[Leader]
What has Diego done?
[Kids]
He's just lost his notebook!

[Leader]
And what has Maya done?
[Kids]
She has broken the lamp!

[All]
Forgotten, left and lost and found —
'have' plus the third one, that's the sound!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
I've forgotten my umbrella,
I have left it on the train.
I have lost it, found it, lost it —
and it's going to rain again.

[Chorus]
Have you done it yet? Not yet!
Have you seen it? Just now!
Already, just and not yet —
the present perfect shows you how!

[Verse 2]
Oliver has broken a string,
Ingrid has already packed.
Maya has just discovered
that the map is inside out — a fact.

[Chorus]
Have you done it yet? Not yet!
Have you seen it? Just now!
Already, just and not yet —
the present perfect shows you how!

[Bridge]
It started then, it matters now:
that's the tense, and that is how.

[Chorus]
Have you done it yet? Not yet!
Have you seen it? Just now!
Already, just and not yet —
the present perfect shows you how!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Touch your shoulder!
[Kids]
Shoulder!

[Leader]
Touch your elbow!
[Kids]
Elbow!

[Leader]
Touch your knee!
[Kids]
Knee! And the back of your neck!

[Leader]
Who has got a beard?
[Kids]
Sven! Ingrid's grandfather!

[All]
Stomach, tongue and finger too —
moustache, back — that's you!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Sven has got a silver beard
and a moustache to match.
Nora's got the strongest shoulders
and a rucksack she can't catch.

[Chorus]
Shoulder, elbow, knee and neck,
stomach, tongue and finger, back!
Say the word and touch the place —
and you will never lose the track!

[Verse 2]
To make friends you use your face,
to take risks you use your knees.
The body does the things you plan
and mostly does them with some ease.

[Chorus]
Shoulder, elbow, knee and neck,
stomach, tongue and finger, back!
Say the word and touch the place —
and you will never lose the track!

[Bridge]
One finger, ten. One knee, two.
Some words change and some don't do.

[Chorus]
Shoulder, elbow, knee and neck,
stomach, tongue and finger, back!
Say the word and touch the place —
and you will never lose the track!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What have you got first?
[Kids]
Maths! Maths and then science!

[Leader]
And after break?
[Kids]
History! And geography!

[Leader]
And on Friday?
[Kids]
Art! Music! Double sport!

[Leader]
And at home?
[Kids]
Homework! Always homework!

[All]
Check the timetable, don't be late —
break at eleven, that's the date!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Maya studies science first,
then geography at ten.
Maths before the morning break
and history again.

[Chorus]
She studies, he studies,
we all do art on Wednesday!
Check the timetable, know it well —
and Friday is a double sport day!

[Verse 2]
In geography this term we're learning
about pollution in the bay,
deforestation up the river
and what we throw away.

[Chorus]
She studies, he studies,
we all do art on Wednesday!
Check the timetable, know it well —
and Friday is a double sport day!

[Bridge]
One little 's' when it's he or she:
she studies, and he studies free.

[Chorus]
She studies, he studies,
we all do art on Wednesday!
Check the timetable, know it well —
and Friday is a double sport day!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
I've got a headache.
[Kids]
You should rest! You should drink water!

[Leader]
I've got a cough.
[Kids]
You should stay warm!

[Leader]
I've got a temperature.
[Kids]
You should see the doctor!

[Leader]
Should I run five kilometres?
[Kids]
No! You shouldn't! Definitely not!

[All]
Toothache, cold and medicine —
the chemist's open, off you go!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
What's the matter, are you ill?
You've got a temperature, I'd say.
You should go and see the doctor,
you shouldn't go to school today.

[Chorus]
You should rest, you shouldn't worry,
you should tell somebody when it hurts!
Medicine and time and water —
that's the order, that's what works!

[Verse 2]
A toothache needs the dentist,
a cold just needs a week.
The vaccination in the autumn
stops the symptoms before they speak.

[Chorus]
You should rest, you shouldn't worry,
you should tell somebody when it hurts!
Medicine and time and water —
that's the order, that's what works!

[Bridge]
'Should' is advice, not an order:
it's a friend, not a border.

[Chorus]
You should rest, you shouldn't worry,
you should tell somebody when it hurts!
Medicine and time and water —
that's the order, that's what works!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Sugar — how much or how many?
[Kids]
How MUCH! You can't count sugar!

[Leader]
Snacks — how much or how many?
[Kids]
How MANY! One, two, three!

[Leader]
Honey?
[Kids]
How much! A spoon of honey!

[Leader]
And flour?
[Kids]
How much! Two cups of flour!

[All]
Butter, cereal, salt and pepper —
jam and yoghurt, count them never!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
A spoon of honey in the yoghurt,
a little salt, a lot of bread.
Some cereal for the morning
and some pepper, Ingrid said.

[Chorus]
How much sugar? How many snacks?
One you count and one you don't!
Butter, flour, jam and honey —
count them and you won't!

[Verse 2]
We exercise on Tuesday evenings,
Maya likes to meditate.
A balanced plate and moving daily
beats a diet any date.

[Chorus]
How much sugar? How many snacks?
One you count and one you don't!
Butter, flour, jam and honey —
count them and you won't!

[Bridge]
One apple, two. But never 'two rice' —
some things just don't split up nice.

[Chorus]
How much sugar? How many snacks?
One you count and one you don't!
Butter, flour, jam and honey —
count them and you won't!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Have we got any cheese?
[Kids]
Yes! We've got some cheese!

[Leader]
Have we got any olives?
[Kids]
No! We haven't got any!

[Leader]
Cut the onion!
[Kids]
Cutting! Cutting!

[Leader]
Add the tomato and mix!
[Kids]
Adding! Mixing! Ready!

[All]
Mushroom, oven, cut and add —
twenty minutes, not too bad!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Have we got any mushrooms?
We've got some, I think, somewhere.
Cut the onion, add the cheese,
and mix it all with care.

[Chorus]
Some and any, cut and mix,
add it, then it's done!
Into the oven, twenty minutes —
pizza for everyone!

[Verse 2]
Diego's making a report
on migration and on rights.
He types it while the oven works
and works most Thursday nights.

[Chorus]
Some and any, cut and mix,
add it, then it's done!
Into the oven, twenty minutes —
pizza for everyone!

[Bridge]
'Some' when you have. 'Any' when you ask.
Two small words, one small task.

[Chorus]
Some and any, cut and mix,
add it, then it's done!
Into the oven, twenty minutes —
pizza for everyone!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Where's the bike?
[Kids]
In the basement! Down the stairs!

[Leader]
Where's the washing?
[Kids]
On the balcony! In the wind!

[Leader]
Where's the milk?
[Kids]
In the fridge! Behind the door!

[Leader]
And where's Kili?
[Kids]
On the roof! On the roof again!

[All]
Lift and gate and shelf and corner —
cupboard, stairs — the house is ours!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The bike is in the basement,
the boots are by the gate.
The jam is on the second shelf
behind the biggest plate.

[Chorus]
Up the stairs or in the lift,
on the balcony, in the corner!
Say exactly where it is
and nobody's a mourner!

[Verse 2]
Mr Vega has a schedule,
every deadline in a row.
He knows which cupboard holds the keys
and which roof lets in snow.

[Chorus]
Up the stairs or in the lift,
on the balcony, in the corner!
Say exactly where it is
and nobody's a mourner!

[Bridge]
Kili the condor lands on the roof
and never, ever lands with proof.

[Chorus]
Up the stairs or in the lift,
on the balcony, in the corner!
Say exactly where it is
and nobody's a mourner!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Whose coat is this?
[Kids]
Mine! It's mine!

[Leader]
Whose is that one?
[Kids]
Yours! That one's yours!

[Leader]
Whose are these?
[Kids]
Hers! They're Maya's!

[Leader]
And whose is the whole expedition?
[Kids]
OURS! It belongs to all of us!

[All]
His and hers and theirs and ours —
whose it is, we know for sure!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Whose notebook has the coffee stain?
It's Diego's, that's for sure.
Whose gloves are on the radiator?
They're Ingrid's, and one more.

[Chorus]
Mine and yours and his and hers,
ours and theirs — whose is it?
Everything belongs to somebody
and some things belong to all of it!

[Verse 2]
Stress belongs to nobody
but visits everyone.
Anxiety says you're alone —
resilience says you're not, and never was.

[Chorus]
Mine and yours and his and hers,
ours and theirs — whose is it?
Everything belongs to somebody
and some things belong to all of it!

[Bridge]
Wellbeing isn't something bought.
It's shared, and that's the thought.

[Chorus]
Mine and yours and his and hers,
ours and theirs — whose is it?
Everything belongs to somebody
and some things belong to all of it!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What does a journalist do?
[Kids]
She writes! She asks! She listens!

[Leader]
What does an engineer do?
[Kids]
He builds! He measures! He checks!

[Leader]
What does a nurse do?
[Kids]
She helps! Every single day!

[Leader]
And a pilot?
[Kids]
He flies! Above the clouds!

[All]
Dentist, waiter, cook and manager —
firefighter, police officer!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The journalist asks the questions,
the engineer draws the plan.
The firefighter runs towards it
when everybody else ran.

[Chorus]
She works, he works, one little 's' —
that's all the difference there!
Nurse and pilot, cook and dentist,
somebody everywhere!

[Verse 2]
Diego realised something
when he interviewed them all:
they discovered what they loved
and then they answered the call.

[Chorus]
She works, he works, one little 's' —
that's all the difference there!
Nurse and pilot, cook and dentist,
somebody everywhere!

[Bridge]
The manager, the waiter,
the police officer at the door.

[Chorus]
She works, he works, one little 's' —
that's all the difference there!
Nurse and pilot, cook and dentist,
somebody everywhere!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Will you travel?
[Kids]
I will! I will travel far!

[Leader]
Will you be famous?
[Kids]
Maybe! Maybe I will!

[Leader]
Will you be an astronaut?
[Kids]
Maya will! Maya will!

[Leader]
Will you forget your friends?
[Kids]
I won't! I never will!

[All]
Artist, singer, scientist, dream —
university, footballer, team!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Maya says she'll be a scientist,
Oliver will be a singer, loud.
Diego will report from somewhere
and make his whole town proud.

[Chorus]
I will, I won't, I might one day —
the future's a very long word!
Astronaut or artist, footballer or teacher,
and every dream gets heard!

[Verse 2]
Ingrid will go to university
and study how the ice behaves.
She'll travel there regularly
and occasionally send waves.

[Chorus]
I will, I won't, I might one day —
the future's a very long word!
Astronaut or artist, footballer or teacher,
and every dream gets heard!

[Bridge]
Whatever you become, I won't forget
who you were before you got there yet.

[Chorus]
I will, I won't, I might one day —
the future's a very long word!
Astronaut or artist, footballer or teacher,
and every dream gets heard!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
How do you get there?
[Kids]
By tram! We go by tram!

[Leader]
How do you get there?
[Kids]
By taxi! Pedro's taxi!

[Leader]
How do you get there?
[Kids]
By bicycle! Along the railway!

[Leader]
And in an emergency?
[Kids]
Ambulance! Fire engine! Move!

[All]
Platform, motorway, traffic, sign —
helicopter, right on time!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
We waited on the platform
for a train that never came.
The motorway was full of traffic
and the tram was much the same.

[Chorus]
By tram, by taxi, by bicycle, by train —
how do you get around?
The railway or the motorway,
above or underground!

[Verse 2]
A bicycle makes almost nothing:
no smoke and hardly any sound.
Renewable energy is coming
and our carbon footprint's coming down.

[Chorus]
By tram, by taxi, by bicycle, by train —
how do you get around?
The railway or the motorway,
above or underground!

[Bridge]
An ambulance, a fire engine,
a helicopter overhead.

[Chorus]
By tram, by taxi, by bicycle, by train —
how do you get around?
The railway or the motorway,
above or underground!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Go straight on!
[Kids]
Straight on! Past the bank!

[Leader]
Turn left!
[Kids]
Left! Along the river!

[Leader]
Go over the bridge!
[Kids]
Over! And through the park!

[Leader]
And where is it?
[Kids]
Opposite the school! Next to the corner!

[All]
Left and right and straight and past —
say it clearly, say it fast!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Go along the river path
and over the old stone bridge.
Turn right and go straight on
until you reach the ridge.

[Chorus]
Left, right, straight on, past,
along and over and through!
Opposite the school, next to the corner —
that's the place for you!

[Verse 2]
This town is diverse and busy,
multicultural and wide.
Ask in any language
and somebody will guide.

[Chorus]
Left, right, straight on, past,
along and over and through!
Opposite the school, next to the corner —
that's the place for you!

[Bridge]
Directions are a kindness:
a stranger who is not lost twice.

[Chorus]
Left, right, straight on, past,
along and over and through!
Opposite the school, next to the corner —
that's the place for you!
